'''George Casella''' (January 22, 1951 – June 17, 2012) was a Distinguished Professor in the Department of Statistics at the [[University of Florida]]. He died from [[multiple myeloma]].<ref name=IMSBulletin />

== Academic career ==
Casella completed his undergraduate education at [[Fordham University]] and graduate education at [[Purdue University]]. He served on the faculty of [[Rutgers University]], [[Cornell University]], and the [[University of Florida]]. His contributions focused on the area of statistics including [[Monte Carlo method]]s, [[model selection]], and [[genomics|genomic analysis]].<ref name=IMSBulletin>{{Cite journal | journal = IMS Bulletin | date = Feb 27, 2013 | title = Obituary: George Casella, 1951-2012 | publisher = [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] | url = http://bulletin.imstat.org/2013/02/obituary-george-casella-1951-2012 | access-date = March 27, 2013 | archive-date = March 6, 2013 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20130306225102/http://bulletin.imstat.org/2013/02/obituary-george-casella-1951-2012/ | url-status = dead }}</ref> He was particularly active in [[Bayesian]] and [[empirical Bayes]] methods, with works connecting with the [[Stein phenomenon]], on assessing and accelerating the convergence of [[Markov chain Monte Carlo]] methods, as in his [[Rao–Blackwellization]] technique,<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Casella|first1=G|title=Rao-Blackwellisation of sampling schemes|journal=Biometrika|volume=83|issue=1|year=1996|pages=81–94|url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/229100766|doi=10.1093/biomet/83.1.81|jstor=2337434}}</ref> and recasting [[lasso (statistics)|lasso]] as [[Maximum a posteriori estimation|Bayesian posterior mode estimation]] with independent [[Laplace distribution|Laplace]] priors.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Park|first1=Trevor|last2=Casella|first2=George|title=The Bayesian Lasso|journal=Journal of the American Statistical Association|volume=103|issue=482|year=2008|pages=681–686|doi=10.1198/016214508000000337|s2cid=11797924|url=http://www.stat.ufl.edu/archived/casella/Papers/Lasso.pdf|access-date=2014-11-07|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180205024436/http://www.stat.ufl.edu/archived/casella/Papers/Lasso.pdf|archive-date=2018-02-05|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Awards ==
Casella was named as a Fellow of the [[American Statistical Association]] and the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] in 1988, and he was made an Elected Fellow of the [[International Statistical Institute]] in 1989. In 2009, he was made a Foreign Member of the [[Spanish Royal Academy of Sciences]].<ref name=CV>{{cite web|last=Casella|first=George|title=VITA|url=http://www.stat.ufl.edu/~casella/Vita11.pdf|accessdate=4 November 2012}}</ref>
